summary:
Monday 10/26 CT list at St. Brigid Imaging (7 bookings) prepared under RBC-RAD-07.

- 08:00 Britt Mohr (pt-0047), CT abdomen/pelvis with contrast. Ordered the CT (sr-t0001). He has diabetes and his last creatinine (9/24) is more than 30 days old, so I ordered a creatinine to be drawn before the scan (sr-t0007). He has no contrast reaction and does not take metformin. Patient messaged.
- 09:00 Daniel Ferreira (pt-0015), CT abdomen/pelvis with contrast. Ordered the CT (sr-t0002). The radiology report from the day of his 2019 reaction grades it moderate (hives and eyelid swelling). The allergy list says "anaphylaxis (patient report)", but under the policy that does not change the grade. Ordered prednisone 50 mg at 20:00 on 10/25, 02:00 and 08:00 on 10/26 (mr-t0010), plus diphenhydramine 50 mg at 08:00 (mr-t0011). His 10/14 creatinine is fine (eGFR 86). He was sent instructions in Spanish and English, including that he needs a driver.
- 10:00 Jamaal Schmitt (pt-0048), CT with contrast. NOT ordered. The 2023 radiology report shows a severe reaction (anaphylaxis with low blood pressure, treated with epinephrine). So there is no contrast, no substitute study and no premedication. I sent an urgent message to radiologist Dr. Adeyemi (comm-t0021) asking him to decide what to do instead. Your follow-up task (task-t0030) is due 10/24, because the patient was told the office will call him before Monday with the plan. I also corrected his allergy entry from mild/low criticality to anaphylaxis/high, citing the report.
- 11:00 Eduardo Stracke (pt-0012), CT abdomen/pelvis with contrast. Ordered the CT (sr-t0003). His 10/13 creatinine of 2.85 gives an eGFR of 24.5 (CKD-EPI 2021). Ordered 500 mL IV normal saline at 10:00 (mr-t0012). He is on insulin, not metformin. Told to arrive at 10:00. His problem list says CKD stage 3, but an eGFR of 24.5 is below that, so the staging is worth reviewing.
- 13:00 Anisha Schuster (pt-0049), CT abdomen/pelvis with contrast. Ordered the CT (sr-t0004). Her ED visit on 10/04 recorded acute kidney injury, and it was not documented as back to baseline, so I treated it as still present. Ordered:
  - a creatinine before the scan (sr-t0008)
  - 500 mL IV normal saline at 12:00 (mr-t0013)
  - a hold on metformin mr-00392: no doses on 10/26 or for 48 hours after the scan
  - a repeat creatinine for 10/28–10/30 (sr-t0017), with a review task for you to decide on restarting metformin (task-t0019). Patient messaged.
- 14:00 Lauren Beahan (pt-0046), CT abdomen/pelvis without contrast (stone protocol). Ordered as booked (sr-t0005). Patient told no preparation is needed.
- 15:00 Salvador Brakus (pt-0050), CT abdomen with contrast (adrenal protocol). Ordered the CT (sr-t0006). His creatinine rose from 0.98 to 1.64 within 48 hours (acute kidney injury, after ibuprofen and vomiting), so the 10/21 value doesn't count. Ordered:
  - a new creatinine before the scan (sr-t0009)
  - 500 mL IV normal saline at 14:00 (mr-t0014)
  - a hold on metformin mr-00398, starting now and lasting until 48 hours after the scan
  - a repeat creatinine for 10/28–10/30 (sr-t0018), with a review task for you (task-t0020). Patient messaged and told to avoid ibuprofen and similar pain relievers.

Each CT order is linked to its appointment, and the radiologist reviews the pre-scan creatinines on the day of the scan. Each patient has a signed chart note citing RBC-RAD-07.

evidence.quote:
1. Sunday 10/25 at 8:00 PM: prednisone 50 mg (1 tablet).
2. Monday 10/26 at 2:00 AM (set an alarm): prednisone 50 mg (1 tablet).
3. Monday 10/26 at 8:00 AM: prednisone 50 mg (1 tablet) AND diphenhydramine (Benadryl) 50 mg (1 capsule).
Diphenhydramine makes you drowsy: do NOT drive on Monday after taking it. Someone must drive you to and from the scan.
